job.style: a news-style report about a real-world situation

response.passage: In the bustling city of Bengaluru, local authorities recently launched a campaign to address the growing crisis of plastic waste clogging urban drains. While many residents believe that plastic litter is merely an aesthetic issue, it actually causes severe waterlogging by blocking drainage systems during monsoon rains. A common mistake is assuming that plastic is a single, uniform substance; in reality, there are many different types of polymers, each requiring specific processing. Many citizens mistakenly throw all types of plastic into a single recycling bin, assuming they can all be processed together. However, mixing different types of dirty plastic makes the recycling process impossible, as contaminants ruin the batch. Furthermore, some residents continue to burn plastic waste in their backyards, wrongly believing that the smoke is harmless, similar to burning wood. In truth, burning plastic releases toxic chemicals into the air, posing serious health risks. Additionally, many people buy products labeled 'biodegradable' thinking they will rot quickly in a standard dustbin. Unfortunately, these materials often require specific industrial conditions to break down and will persist for years if simply discarded in a landfill or the ocean. Understanding that plastic is a complex, synthetic material that does not simply vanish is the first step toward effective waste management.
response.summary: Plastic waste in cities causes major environmental and health problems due to improper disposal and misconceptions. Residents must learn that not all plastics are the same and that burning or mixing them is harmful.
